description:
Found by s527a's corpus-diff (2026-10-24), PRE-EXISTING and independent of the PPI in use: the emission of perl-tests/hash.t depends on whether the PROTOTYPE CACHE (Pl::ProtoCache) is cold or warm.  The #2610 detector table row for line 116's `Hash::Util::bucket_ratio` reads `"unknown"` on a cold cache and `"list-call"` on a warm one -- with the installed PPI 1.291 (PCL_SYSTEM_PPI=1) exactly as with the vendored one.

Reproducer (scratch/s527a/bin/hash-cache.sh in the s527a worktree): a fresh private PCL_CACHE_DIR (chmod 700), `./pl2cl perl-tests/hash.t | grep -o 'bucket_ratio" 116 "[a-z-]*"'` twice:
  cold: bucket_ratio" 116 "unknown"
  warm: bucket_ratio" 116 "list-call"
The source: `require Hash::Util; sub Hash::Util::bucket_ratio (\%); ... Hash::Util::bucket_ratio(%$h)` (hash.t:137-141).

Why it matters: a transpile is supposed to be a function of its inputs; a cold/warm difference makes corpus-diff report a diff that no code change caused (s527a saw it as the ONE non-@INC difference over 111 files, because corpus-diff's REF side runs from a fresh worktree whose compiler stamp has a cold cache) and means a cached prototype fact reaches the emission in a way the cold path does not reproduce (the standing rule: an emission that depends on cached state must be keyed by it, or computed the same way cold).  Discriminating measurement for the fix: dump the facts the detector consults for `bucket_ratio` on the cold and the warm run (which side holds the `(\%)` prototype: the in-file forward declaration or the cached Hash::Util facts) -- the warm answer is the one a fresh process should also give if the forward declaration is visible.
subject: Emission depends on a cold vs warm prototype cache: hash.t detector row for Hash::Util::bucket_ratio reads unknown cold, list-call warm (pre-existing, PPI-independent)
